vulnerabilities.description: Predictable Session ID Generation - Using Date.now() for session IDs is not cryptographically secure. Attackers can easily predict session IDs and hijack sessions. Requires 'crypto.randomBytes()' instead.
No Session Expiration Logic - Sessions are persisted indefinitely with no TTL or expiration mechanism. Stale sessions can be replayed by attackers.
Unencrypted Session Storage - Session data including context is stored in plaintext JSON files. Sensitive session data should be encrypted at rest.
Insufficient Input Validation - Keys and values are accepted without validation. No checks for path traversal sequences or other malicious input patterns.
Silent JSON Parse Failure - loadMemory() silently returns empty object on JSON parse errors. This masks data corruption or injection attacks.
No Access Control - Memory and session helpers lack authentication/authorization. Any process with file access can read/write all data.
Potential Information Disclosure - Multiple database path candidates are probed, potentially revealing filesystem structure information in error logs.

recommendations: Replace Date.now() session ID generation with crypto.randomBytes(32) for cryptographically secure random IDs
Implement session TTL with automatic expiration (e.g., 1 hour idle timeout, 24 hour max lifetime)
Encrypt sensitive session data using crypto.createCipheriv() with AES-256-GCM
Add input validation for memory keys (whitelist alphanumeric + underscore/dash patterns)
Update JSON.parse() to throw errors instead of silently failing; log parse errors for security monitoring
Consider using fs.promises with restricted file permissions (chmod 0600) for sensitive files
Implement RBAC or at minimum filesystem-level access controls on .claude-flow directory
Add rate limiting to prevent brute-force session enumeration attacks
Audit all shell command execution - verified that execFileSync with array args (github-safe.js) is correctly implemented
No hardcoded secrets detected - maintain this practice and use environment variables for all credentials
